page: Amazon Web Services m7a.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores utilizing the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9R14 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark results place this instance in the top tier for multi-core CPU performance, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks also ranks in the top tier, while large block read and write operations fall into the strong category. Single-core performance is strong, though certain workloads like single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression perform at an average level.

The instance demonstrates strong capabilities for database operations, redis SET transactions, and static web serving. It also achieves top-tier text generation speeds for medium-sized LLM models. Given the dedicated core allocation and DDR5 memory architecture, the m7a.16xlarge offers high resource density and compute-to-memory balance, making it suitable for enterprise applications, software compilation pipelines, and memory-bound database workloads that do not require local NVMe storage.
